sentences.text: My old dog walks slowly up the green hill.
I spread sweet honey on my warm fresh bread.
I went out to play though it looked like it was going to rain.

When I am in bed, I hear soft sounds outside my room. The wind blows, and I start to feel sleepy. Mum reads to herself, while Dad sings softly to himself. In an instant, my eyes begin to close. I do not feel restless anymore. The soft sounds help me drift off to sleep.

A new girl joined our class from a foreign country. Her hair was longer than mine, and she had a warm smile. We discuss our history and culture at lunch. She taught me new words, and I taught her some too. We express our ideas and develop a secret hand sign. One benefit of a new friend is learning from each other. We are likely to be good friends for a long time.
My parents went to school for the big meeting.
Spring is the best season of the whole year.
We drink cool water from the clear little stream.

Our class went on a nature search in a wild region near our town. We walked beside a stream to find its source. The current was strong and cold. I brought a book to draw what I saw. We covered a long path and found more than thirty kinds of plants and birds. We examined them and selected a few to draw. I arranged my pictures when we got back. It was not a normal school day because it involved learning outdoors.

On clear nights, Dad and I observe the stars. We collect facts about the ones we know. I connect the bright spots to make shapes and compare the big stars with the small ones. Dad helps me measure the space between them. There are so many that I wonder how far their light must travel to reach us. Perhaps one day, I will see them up close!
My sister made the pink cake all by herself.
I came in second place in the running race.
I draw a picture of my brown dog for grandma.

There was a race at school today. I was already excited when my family came to cheer for me. I ran as fast as I could and made a new school record! My teacher gave me a silver cup, and Dad took a picture. I am looking forward to next year. Nothing can stop me from trying my best!

I wrote a card to Grandma today. I told her that I came second in my spelling test. In the middle, I drew a funny monkey. I posted the card by myself. I wonder what Grandma will think the moment she sees it. Maybe she will notice how much my writing has improved!
Please wait here for a moment while I get my bag.
The days grow longer in the middle of the summer.
Nobody was home so I played with my dog outside.

Last year, we went on a trip to see winter for the first time! From our window, I watched the white snow cover the whole street. The trees looked quiet and the world seemed still. My mother made warm milk for us. We would listen to music in the living room. My brother read a chapter of his book. Winter is a lovely season to spend with family. I would not change a single thing!

My teacher asked me to give a speech in English class. I chose to report on the natural world and explain how a spring can become part of a river. I looked at my notes once, then spoke slowly and gave an example. Nobody made a sound while I spoke. My method was simple: believe in myself and speak clearly. The result was better than I expected! My teacher said I should repeat this again one day.
I would love to visit a foreign country one day.
It is natural for birds to fly south in winter.
My brother built the model boat all by himself.

Our class has a council once a month. Every child has the same rights and a chance to speak. This month, we have a reason to meet. Our book box is always messy! We make a new policy: please put each book back in the right place. Within a few minutes, we all agree. We hope our books will remain neat from now on.

Our class planted a young tree in the school yard. Trees give us oxygen and help our planet. Our teacher told us a theory that trees can help reduce heat on a street. I can relate to that because I love sitting under a cool tree! We return each day to water it, and we are certain it will grow tall. Caring for our tree shows our concern for the Earth.
The kind officer helped me cross the busy street.
My dad knows how to operate the big machine.
The soft brown rabbit hops around in the garden.

It was a warm day by the sea. There were almost a hundred people there. Dad and I took turns jumping into the water. On my first attempt, I made the biggest splash! The water spread out in a wide pattern and flew towards Mum. It caught her square on the back, and she laughed. Between each jump, we swam a little further. However tired we were, we still had time for another minute of fun. Finally, we said goodbye to the sea and went home.

We have a modern washing machine next to our kitchen. It helps clean our clothes while we do other things. A century ago, washing clothes took much more work. Modern machines improve our lives in a million simple ways. Instead of spending a long time washing, we have more time together. Every member of my family helps with the chores at home.
We travel to the sea by train every year.
We spend the evening in the living room.
The opposing team is strong in their defence.

Every week, Mum and I visit the local market in the morning. People sell fresh bread, warm cookies and sweet fruit. I carry the basket and help Mum choose a nice orange. My little sister picks a pretty flower for Grandpa. A kind person gives us an extra apple for free! On the way home, we hear the birds sing. I really love spending time with my family. It is a perfect start to the week!

Every summer, our garden is full of colour. Purple and gold flowers grow along the wall. A rabbit hops across the grass in the evening. Mum has a simple system for watering each plant in the right order. I follow her around and help where I can. Together, we keep our garden happy and healthy.
We finally arrived at the sea after the long trip.
I select the biggest red apple from the basket.
I know I should water the plants every morning.

Our band will perform in the parade this year. I manage the beat while my friend plays the melody. The music puts the whole street in motion. A police officer smiles as we march past her office. People from all over the nation come to watch. Mr Ray gives the big bell a strike at just the right time. We play for one full period, and no matter how tired we get, the parade still feels magical.

On a recent trip, we visited a farm near our town. The farmers showed us how they operate their big machines. Some wheels were taller than me! The farm grows a large supply of corn and keeps cows for milk. A company buys some of the food and sends it as far as America. Our guide told us how farms help the economy and educate people about caring for the land. I never knew one farm could help feed so many people!
